captions.en: The relationship between politics and money has been, across time and place, an enduring issue of democracy.
A politician swears to represent the will of the voters.
But in reality, they are bound by the source of campaign funds.
Whether Democrat or Republican, political activity costs large sums of money.
Where to obtain these funds becomes the issue.
Corporate donations have long been a subject of dispute.
If a company donates money, it expects policies favorable to that company.
Corporate support may therefore carry an implied expectation.
Cases of corruption and bribery have brought down many ministers and lawmakers.
The anger of the public demands strict punishment for corrupt politicians.
A maximum ceiling on donations, the duty of disclosure, examination of how money is spent.
But methods that circumvent the regulatory net keep being developed.
Political funding organizations and fundraising events can create many loopholes.
To ensure true democracy, the setting up of institutions alone is inadequate.
Public scrutiny, investigative reporting of the media, and the involvement of voters are indispensable.
For a vote to carry meaning, citizens must also accept the responsibility of watching politics closely.
